# Discrete Mathematics Laboratories

Six discrete-maths lab deliverables for a Master's course at Wrocław University of Science and
Technology, each turned into a **runnable artifact** rather than a write-up. 108 files, single author,
MIT, public remote. The organising idea is stated in the repo itself and is the reason this repo gets
its own pattern page — see [[make-the-formal-object-observable]].

> "The thread running through all six: take a formal object (a cut, a modulus, a set, a recursion, a
> graph, an information system) and make its behaviour **observable**."
> — Discrete-Mathematics-Laboratories/README.md, 2026-07-10

**Status: coursework, finished and frozen at last commit 2026-07-10.** The course is done and nothing
is maintained ("All finished and frozen" — interview, 2026-07-28).

## The six labs

| Lab | Topic | Stack | Concept pages |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lab1_Max_Cut` | Max-Cut, NP-hard partitioning | Python stdlib | [[max-cut-and-local-search]] |
| `lab2_Crypt` | RSA keygen + four factorization attacks | Jupyter/Colab, numpy, [[matplotlib]] | [[rsa-and-integer-factorization]] |
| `lab3_Sets` | Set theory as a library; job recommender | Python, no deps | [[characteristic-functions]] · [[set-similarity-metrics]] |
| `lab4_Complexity` | Ackermann, Stirling, Nim — twice (Python + browser) | [[matplotlib]], [[tkinter]], vanilla JS | [[ackermann-and-primitive-recursion]] · [[sprague-grundy-nim-sum]] |
| `lab5_GraphTheory` | SentinelNet (Iberian grid) + Q-HYDRO Wrocław (gravimeter mesh) | [[react]] vendored; Leaflet | [[shortest-path-algorithm-family]] · [[graph-connectivity-and-resilience]] |
| `lab6_Neo4j` | Pawlak information system `S=(U,A)` | [[neo4j]], [[cypher]], plus an offline JS viewer | [[pawlak-information-system]] |

Directory numbering carries the course order and the root README walks them as chapters — the local
variant of [[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]]. Labs 4 (part 2), 5 and 6 (viewer) are double-click
HTML, see [[offline-first-static-deliverable]]. Lab 4 and lab 6 each exist twice in two stacks:
[[dual-implementation-as-cross-check]].

## Git history — this repo *contradicts* the usual pattern

49 commits, **2026-03-20 → 2026-07-10**, five working dates with real gaps, and commits that only
exist because something broke: `48ba16d Fix UnicodeEncodeError in the lab3 demos on Windows consoles`,
`06b5882 Make SentinelNet run offline: vendor React, precompile the JSX` (2,692 insertions),
`8a2acfe Add .gitignore and stop tracking compiled bytecode`, `e42bc80 Rename Max_Cut_lab1 to
lab1_Max_Cut`. That is a working log, not an import — a documented counter-example to
[[import-finished-work-into-git]].

**Caveat, so the wiki does not overstate it:** *within-session* granularity is still upload-shaped.
Whole finished labs land in one day, one commit per file with the file path as the message, and one
commit is literally `Add files via upload` from the GitHub web UI. Finished work still gets imported —
just repeatedly, over four months, with fixes in between.

The 2026-07-10 tail is a textbook publishing pass — seven README+screenshot commits, then
`0a6d54b Rewrite the top-level README as a guided tour`, `24e7b33 Add MIT license`, `7273d68 Add
license badges`. See [[presentation-polish-tail-commits]] and [[readme-as-guided-tour]].
Per the interview these bursts were "just cleaning up local folders" — consolidation, not a release.

**Provenance note.** `brain.py survey` reported this repo as first = last = 2026-07-10, hiding the
whole four-month arc. Every date above came from `git log` directly; the survey's git dates are not
trustworthy.

## Findings

- **`tspChristofides` in `sn-algo.js` is not Christofides.** It matches odd-degree vertices greedily
  rather than by minimum-weight perfect matching, so the 1.5-approximation guarantee does **not**
  hold. Call it a Christofides-*shaped* heuristic. Recorded on
  [[shortest-path-algorithm-family]]. `confidence: high` (read from source).
- **The zero-dependency claim is internally contradicted.** `lab4/part2` and `lab6/viewer` contain
  zero external URLs; `Q-HYDRO Wrocław` says "No dependencies are vendored" and loads Leaflet, map
  tiles and IBM Plex from CDNs. Two lab-5 apps side by side under opposite rules, and the root
  README's "all run offline" overstates it. See [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]].
- **Documentation drift, three instances.** `lab6_Neo4j/guide.txt` still lists "object count = 38"
  after the README says 38→39 was corrected "throughout"; the same file hard-codes a stale personal
  absolute path; the root README's offline claim above. See [[documentation-drift]].
- The only automated check in the repo is `lab3_Sets/mandatory_tasks/test_suite.py`, a hand-rolled
  `TestRunner` with boolean assertions — not [[pytest]]. Everything else is asserted in prose and
  screenshots.
- Boundaries are written beside the claims rather than hidden — "a conservative placeholder — a full
  Stoer-Wagner cut is out of scope", "swap in a binary heap for scale". This is the strongest
  instance of [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] in the whole source set.
- `lab6_Neo4j/guide.txt` is written as an assistant addressing the user and closes *"When all are in
  this folder, say \"screenshots ready\" -> I build the LaTeX report."* — a handoff instruction
  shipped as a lab deliverable. No agent tooling is in the tree: no `.tooling/`, no `CLAUDE.md`, no
  CI. Do not infer any.
- No `.gitattributes` and no Git LFS: 19 PNGs and an 840 KB PDF are committed as plain blobs.
